subject: Mapping two variables to the same aesthetic on different layers end up overriding each other

messages.author: 980f46a66dfc8362
messages.subject: Mapping two variables to the same aesthetic on different layers end up overriding each other
parts:
Hi,
I'm trying to generate a plot with two layers (geom_segment and geom_point), which get their data from two data frames.
The problem is that when I try to set the same aesthetic (e.g. size) in both layers (referring to different columns in their data frames) one overrides the other.

e.g

 ggplot()  +
    geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = X1, y = X2, xend = X1.1, yend = X2.1, size = Weight)) +
    geom_point(data = coords, aes(X1, X2, size = Numbers))



Is there a way of mapping two different variables to the same aesthetic on different layers?

Minimal example:

edges <- data.frame(X1 = rep(0, 6), X2 = rep(0, 6), X1.1 = seq(1, 6), X2.1 = seq(6, 1), weight = runif(6, min = 0, max = 1))
coords <- data.frame(X1 = seq(1, 6), X2 = seq(6, 1), numbers = runif(6, min = 10, max = 100))

compare:

ggplot()  +
    geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = X1, y = X2, xend = X1.1, yend = X2.1, size = weight))

    geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = X1, y = X2, xend = X1.1, yend = X2.1, size = weight)) +
    geom_point(data = coords, aes(X1, X2, size = numbers))

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Mapping two variables to the same aesthetic on different layers end up overriding each other
parts:
On Tue, Oct 13, 2015 at 11:26 AM, Roey Angel <roey....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Brian, but that's not what I meant.
> The minimal example I provided doesn't fully show it but I really need to
> draw data from two data frames of different size, so your solution doesn't
> help I'm afraid.
> The problem this minimal example is trying to show is that the circle size
> overrides the segment width, while the legend is just completely mixed up.

That's not actually what happens. You can't have multiple size
legends, there can be only one. So when you map multiple variables to
size, you get a combined legend for the two mappings. On the scale of
the numbers column the weight values are all indistinguishably small,
so the segments all have indistinguishably similar sizes. All this is
as designed in ggplot2; as Brian said, you pretty much can't/shouldn't
map multiple different things to a single aesthetic in ggplot2. Your
best bet is to use some other aesthetic to represent either weight or
number, e.g.,

ggplot() +
geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = X1, y = X2, xend = X1.1, yend =
X2.1, size = weight)) +

geom_point(data = coords, aes(X1, X2, color = numbers))

Best,
Ista

parts: Or rescale the variables to the same scale and plot them. Not sure how you would make the legend make sense though. You could use cut() to make a factor based upon the new scale and change labels in the legend to ranges per variable, but that gets complicated quickly and you lose clarity.

On Tue, Oct 13, 2015 at 12:02 Ista Zahn <ista...@gmail.com> wrote:
On Tue, Oct 13, 2015 at 11:26 AM, Roey Angel <roey....@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Brian, but that's not what I meant.
> The minimal example I provided doesn't fully show it but I really need to
> draw data from two data frames of different size, so your solution doesn't
> help I'm afraid.
> The problem this minimal example is trying to show is that the circle size
> overrides the segment width, while the legend is just completely mixed up.

That's not actually what happens. You can't have multiple size
legends, there can be only one. So when you map multiple variables to
size, you get a combined legend for the two mappings. On the scale of
the numbers column the weight values are all indistinguishably small,
so the segments all have indistinguishably similar sizes. All this is
as designed in ggplot2; as Brian said, you pretty much can't/shouldn't
map multiple different things to a single aesthetic in ggplot2. Your
best bet is to use some other aesthetic to represent either weight or
number, e.g.,

 ggplot()  +
    geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = X1, y = X2, xend = X1.1, yend =
X2.1, size = weight)) +
    geom_point(data = coords, aes(X1, X2, color = numbers))

Best,
Ista
